key_features.classic_presentation: ONSET: Gradual, often post-prandial (after eating). LOCATION: RETROSTERNAL, epigastric, can mimic cardiac pain. RADIATES upward to throat. DURATION: Minutes to hours. CHARACTER: BURNING, rising sensation from stomach. AGGRAVATING: Large meals, fatty foods, spicy foods, lying flat, bending over. RELIEVING: Antacids, sitting upright, PPIs. TIMING: Postprandial, worse at night when lying down. SEVERITY: 3-6/10. KEY POSITIVES: Sour taste, regurgitation, worse after meals, worse lying flat, chronic history, relieved by antacids. KEY NEGATIVES: NOT exertional, NOT radiating to arm/jaw (though can), NOT diaphoresis.

red_flags: New onset in older patient (rule out cardiac)
Radiation to arm or jaw (atypical for GERD)
